task.description: Independently re-verify REQ-227's implementation (Letflow.Entities.Record.Validator) against the validated design and REQ-227's 7 acceptance criteria: idiom, supervision, scope discipline, and decision-record consistency.

result.note: Independently re-ran every cited command; all claims held. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean (Compiling 1 file, no warnings). `mix format --check-formatted`: clean (no output). `mix test test/letflow/entities/record/validator_test.exs`: 'Finished in 0.07 seconds ... Result: 10 passed', 0 failures. Regression: `mix test test/letflow/entities/`: 47 passed, 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/event_store/`: 150 passed, 0 failures. `git diff 3bcfc54a..HEAD --stat` shows exactly three changed paths: handoffs/WF02-REQ227-20260906/step-02-elixir-dev.json (bookkeeping), lib/letflow/entities/record/validator.ex (new, 102 lines), test/letflow/entities/record/validator_test.exs (new, 212 lines) -- no route, no controller, no migration, no REQ-228 event-registration/command code anywhere. Design fidelity confirmed by direct read: module is `Letflow.Entities.Record.Validator` at lib/letflow/entities/record/validator.ex; both functions present with the exact @spec from design §4/§5 (build_record_schema/1, validate_record_payload/2); the field_subschema/1 clauses (lines 91-101) match design §4.1's type-mapping table field-for-field (:string/:integer/:decimal->number/:boolean/:date->string/:datetime->string/:enum->string+enum/:json->%{} with type key omitted); validate_record_payload/2 (line 84-87) calls JsonSchema.validate(field_values, schema) matching JsonSchema.validate/2's actual @spec order (payload, schema) confirmed by reading lib/letflow/event_store/registry/json_schema.ex line 32; namespace decision (a) from design §5.1 followed verbatim -- direct aliases to Letflow.EventStore.Registry.JsonSchema and Letflow.EventStore.Registry.ValidationFailure, no extraction, no adapter module. Violation-shape reuse confirmed: read lib/letflow/event_store/registry/validation_failure.ex directly -- %ValidationFailure{field_path, constraint, actual} is used verbatim by the delegating call, no new struct invented anywhere in validator.ex. All 7 ACs have genuine tests, read directly in test/letflow/entities/record/validator_test.exs: AC1 zero-violations (lines 36-64, three tests: full payload, minimal-required-only payload, six :json-shape variants via a for-loop); AC2 all-violations-not-just-first (lines 73-102, one fixture hitting type+enum+additionalProperties+missing-required simultaneously, asserts all 4 constraint names, all 4 field_paths, and length==4 so nothing short-circuited); AC3 exact (field_path,constraint,actual) triples (lines 111-145, three tests using literal %ValidationFailure{} equality for type/required/enum violations); AC4 engine-reuse (lines 154-181, one test asserting byte-identical output between validate_record_payload/2 and a direct JsonSchema.validate/2 call on the same derived schema, plus a literal-map assertion pinning build_record_schema/1's own output); AC5 namespace decision stated explicitly in design doc §5.1 (verified by reading it, four numbered rationale points); AC6 no route/controller (confirmed directly via the git diff --stat above, not just cited); AC7 mix test/mix compile (confirmed by this review's own independent re-run above, not trusted from the handoff). No SECURITY-REVIEWER gate needed: validator.ex is a pure functional module (confirmed by reading it end-to-end) -- no Repo call, no Ecto.Schema, no GenServer/process, no route/controller/Plug touched, and no tenant-scoped query or write; it operates entirely on in-memory maps passed as arguments, matching REQ-225's own Definition.Validator/Shape precedent (also pure, also ungated by SECURITY-REVIEWER). Idiom/scope review: this is correctly a plain functional module, zero unnecessary abstraction -- no behaviour, no macro, no GenServer wrapping a stateless computation; delegates all constraint-evaluation to the existing JsonSchema.validate/2 rather than reimplementing traversal (confirmed no recursive schema-walking logic exists in validator.ex, only the two functions specified). Cross-namespace alias (Letflow.Entities.* calling Letflow.EventStore.Registry.*) is accepted per design §5.1's explicit, reasoned decision (rule-of-three, existing precedent via Letflow.Definitions.JsonSchemaShape) -- this is a decision-record-consistent choice, not a silent violation of namespace boundaries, and REVIEWER agrees with the reasoning: JsonSchema is a dependency-free pure leaf module, and forcing an extraction now for a second caller would add an indirection layer with zero behavior change. No scope creep found: no behaviour/protocol/macro introduced ahead of need, and the module does not reach into REQ-228 territory (no event registration, no command functions, no Letflow.Entities.Record parent document-shape module invented early -- OQ-3 correctly left as a flag for REQ-228's own design pass rather than acted on here). Type-safety observation (non-blocking, per REVIEWER's own charter item 3): build_record_schema/1's field_subschema/1 (lines 91-101) pattern-matches on %{type: :string} etc. but has no catch-all clause -- if a future field_type() value were added to Definition without updating this private function, the failure mode is a FunctionClauseError inside build_record_schema/1 at record-validation time rather than a compile-time exhaustiveness check. This is not a defect for REQ-227's own scope (field_type/0 is a closed 8-value union today, all 8 covered, confirmed by reading lib/letflow/entities/definition.ex's field_type() type), but is exactly the kind of runtime-only gap ELIXIR-DEV's own §4 note (OQ-1) anticipates for a future field_def() extension. Recorded as a candidate type-safety issue rather than filed as a new docs/issues/ entry, since it requires no action until field_type() is actually extended and Dialyzer (if run) would already flag an unreachable/non-exhaustive private function on such a change -- flagging for ORCH/ELIXIR-DEV awareness rather than blocking this PASS. OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-4 (design doc §8) are all correctly deferred, non-blocking design notes, not defects -- REVIEWER concurs with OQ-1's 'confirmed superset, currently unused' reading and OQ-2's 'rule of three, not yet' reasoning; OQ-4's date/datetime format-inertness is a pre-existing, documented JsonSchema.validate/2 limitation, not introduced by this requirement. Verdict: PASS -- proceed to TEST-DESIGNER (test suite already comprehensive per TEST-DESIGNER's normal charter, but the gate itself is idiom/scope, which this implementation satisfies).
